alex: Hey team — customer 'Rivermark' getting intermittent 429s starting ~00:00 UTC. Saw a sharp spike in RPM/TPS at the same time. Can someone help triage? :eyes:

maria: Which key / app id? Any correlation with cron jobs or SDKs?

alex: api_key=rmk_live_******, app name Rivermark-web. They report ~7200 req/min for 2 minutes then back to normal. No recent deploys on their side.

jamal: That pattern (2-min window) screams top-of-minute aggregation or bursty client loops. Are they using concurrent streaming or many parallel connections?

alex: Customer said they moved from sequential to parallel upload + streaming in last week. SDK v1.4.5.

rate-limiter-bot: [automated] 429 spikes detected for api_key rmk_live_**** between 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z and 2026-03-01T00:03:00Z. Peak RPM=7600, TPMinstant=95.

sophia: Can you paste a sample request/headers and any Retry-After or rate headers from their client logs?

alex: From their logs (redacted):
```
HTTP/2 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-ratelimit-limit: 5000/min
x-rw-ratelimit-remaining: 0
x-rw-ratelimit-reset: 24
retry-after: 15
```
They recorded Retry-After sometimes missing, and some clients got 429 with 0 remaining.

maria: x-rw-ratelimit-limit 5000/min — that matches our per-account minute cap. But their reported peak 7600 > 5000 so we hit the quota. Need to confirm whether ramp is due to many workers or clock alignment.

jamal: Two possibilities: fixed-window vs rolling-window behavior on client side + many parallel connections causing them to exhaust the last tokens in the minute. Also if they have many short-lived connections, keepalive disabled, each connection may send its own warmup.

alex: Repro steps I tried from my laptop: running 200 concurrent processes hitting /v1/generate at 100ms intervals for 90s yields a similar 429 wave. Curl example:
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  (while true; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer rmk_test_***" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate; sleep 0.1; done) &
done
sleep 100
```
This reproduces 429s around the 50-60s mark.

sophia: That reproduces a token-bucket fill/empty across the minute. Two mitigation paths: (1) customer smooths traffic (stagger starts, reduce concurrency), (2) we increase their committed RPM or enable burst allowance for their account temporarily.

maria: Also recommend they enable client-side leaky-bucket smoothing in the SDK: set max_concurrency and request pacing. We should check SDK defaults — v1.4.5 might allow unlimited parallel streams.

jamal: On infra side, confirm we returned Retry-After consistently. If some 429s returned without headers, that's a bug. Also check whether per-route limits vs account-level limit applied — if per-route limit hit, headers might be different.

infra-oncall: I looked at the trace for that api_key. Rate limiter used sliding-window aggregation across edge nodes. I see consistent Retry-After emitted, but a small fraction (~4%) of 429 responses lacked headers due to a short-circuit path when the request was dropped by upstream proxy (we're fixing that).

alex: Customer also reported their retry loop was immediate (no backoff) which amplified the storm. They have an internal retry library that retries on 429 without jitter.

sophia: Action items:
- Ask customer to implement exponential backoff + jitter (recommended 500ms base with jitter) — I can share the snippet.
- Offer a one-time temporary bump to their RPM for the next 48h while they roll out SDK change.
- Infra: patch missing header short-circuit and confirm per-route vs account header clarity.

maria: Snippet for exponential backoff to send to customer:
```
retry_count=0
max=5
while [ $retry_count -lt $max ]; do
  resp=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' ...)
  if [ "$resp" -ne 429 ]; then break; fi
  sleep_time=$(( (1 << retry_count) * 0.5 ))
  jitter=$(awk -v seed="$RANDOM" 'BEGIN{srand(seed); print rand()*0.5}')
  sleep $(echo "$sleep_time + $jitter" | bc)
  retry_count=$((retry_count+1))
done
```

jamal: Also suggested client-side smoothing config for SDK: set max_concurrency=8, per_worker_interval=0.2s, and batch small requests where appropriate. That will keep per-minute steady.

alex: Customer agreed to roll SDK change and will deploy tonight; asked for temporary quota bump.

infra-oncall: I can grant a 2x RPM bump to 10000/min for 48h scoped to their key. I'll also deploy a fix to ensure Retry-After + x-rw-ratelimit-* headers are always set on 429s.

sophia: I'll draft the customer-facing message with suggested SDK flags, the backoff snippet, and the temporary bump details.

alex: Thanks. One more ask — can we add a short doc blurb on "top-of-minute aggregation" with examples? Customer found the concept confusing.

maria: Good idea. I'll add a KB: explain fixed vs rolling windows, mitigation patterns (stagger, smoothing, backoff) and sample SDK configs.

alex: Great — marking this resolved once infra confirms bump + header fix. :white_check_mark: 

rate-limiter-bot: [automated] incident update: quota bump applied to rmk_live_**** until 2026-03-03T00:00:00Z. Patch to header short-circuit merged to staging.

sophia: Leaving final notes here and closing thread once customer confirms post-deploy behavior.

alex: Closing after customer confirms — will follow up in ~24h. :thumbsup:
